To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GLUT1 deficiency syndrome can present as a combination of episodical paroxysmal neurological symptoms and that ketogenic diet is an effective treatment for this condition.

1) we identified two monochoronic twins with a novel missense mutation of SLC21 gene, 2) these patients showed an early-onset and progressive combination of paroxysmal neurological disorders that included paroxysmal dyskinesia and absence epilepsy, and 3) ketogenic diet resulted in an immediate and near-complete resolution of their clinical manifestations.

two monozygotic twins developed, between ages of 5 and 11, a combination of paroxysmal disorders that include paroxysmal dyskinesia and migraine with and without aura, absence epilepsy and writer's cramps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a novel SLC1A2 missense mutation and its association with a combination of neurological disorders.
the study of the molecular mechanisms that underlie the pathogenesis of the paroxysmal neurological events that characterize the GLUT1 Deficiency Syndrome.
the identification of a novel mutation in SLC2A gene in two patients with a combination of paroxysmal neurological events.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a novel GLUT1 deficiency syndrome with a novel SCLC2A1 mutation is associated with episodic exercise-induced dysknesia, migraine without and with aura, absence epilepsy and writer's cramps.
the ketogenic diet may be a useful treatment for a variety of neurological disorders.
a high index suspicion for GLUT1 Deficiency Syndrome (GLUT1-DS) is warranted in patients with multiple episodic neurological disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GLUT1 deficiency syndrome can present as a combination of paroxysmal neurological disorders.
GLUT1 deficiency syndrome should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with a combination of paroxysmal disorders.
a ketogenic diet should be considered in the management of GLUT1 deficiency syndrome, even in patients with a mild CSF/serumn glucose ratio.
